gen-gf-paprika-gf-hammersmith-one: Loud, loose and wide-lettered, Paprika fills the line with lowercase that stands nearly as tall as capitals. And Hammersmith One keeps its rounded, cord-like strokes tight in height, a plain sans that lets the heading do the shouting.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-inder: Inder reads smooth and level, its capitals barely rising above the lowercase around them. Paprika is the one that grabs attention with its spread-out, open-bowled letters, while Inder is the one that quietly carries a plain sans text.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-jaldi: Paprika sets a loud, widely spaced tone, its lowercase filling the line like capitals and its counters hollow and open. But Jaldi follows with brushed, tightly packed sans letters and a tall x-height, so a long passage would feel dense and friendly.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Brash, spacious and full of hollow shapes, Paprika makes the first impression. Then Kdam Thmor Pro, a plain sans with bowls that fill the line, can be sized down a notch without losing its modern punch.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-krona-one: Krona One reads loose and weighty, its lowercase standing up with the stature of cast iron capitals in a friendly sans-serif. Paprika's scattered, open letters are the sharp counterpunch.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-magra: Big, brash and open, Paprika takes the top spot with lowercase that fills the line. Magra holds the plain sans text below, giving every lowercase word a hefty body while Paprika does the showing off.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-major-mono-display: Hollow reeds meet neon glass here, Paprika loud and loose above a wire-thin monospace. But Major Mono Display spaces its tubelike curves so widely that a longer passage would read as precise, technical and slow.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-matemasie: Open on top, closed below. Paprika is best at big, hollow-countered letters that fill a line, whereas Matemasie is best at its broad gaps and curves as thick as its stems, in a tidy sans-serif.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-menbere: Paprika opens with scattered, hollow-countered letters, its lowercase filling the line the way capitals would. Menbere answers by stacking tall lowercase sans letters like rolled cord, a quiet foil.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-momo-trust-display: Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals, with hollow counters spread far apart across each word. Momo Trust Display, a sans-serif with its own drifting letters and generous x-height, echoes that spacing.
